title: DR1 lists the animals already identified in a table with a column per identifier; the frontend squashes each one into a single line reading 'Passport: X, Ear tag: Y'.

finding.frontend: Each animal already entered appears as one summary-list row: the key reads 'Animal 1' and the value is every identifier joined into one string — 'Passport: UK123456789, Ear tag: UK123456789012' — with a Remove action on the right. Records with nothing filled read 'No identifier provided'. The picture is fe-animal-identification-at-maximum, where two cattle read 'Animal 1 — Ear tag: UK123456789012' and 'Animal 2 — Ear tag: UK210987654321' as two `govuk-summary-list` rows; the page holds no table element at all. There is no column, so nothing lines up: a reader comparing the two animals reads each value as a sentence and finds the identifier name inside it. The row is built at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/animal-identification/identifier/summary.js:9-19 and rendered at _identification-card.njk:12-24.
finding.prototype: DR1 shows the same information as a table. The header names the identifiers the commodity asks for, so a cattle panel heads its columns Animal, Ear tag, Passport; each saved animal is one row, labelled with the species name and its number — 'Syncerus spp. 1' — with its values under the matching columns and a Remove button in the last cell (app/routes.js:1802-1820). A person scanning for a missing ear tag reads down one column.
finding.difference: Replace the summary list with a table whose columns are the identifier fields in scope for that commodity line, one row per saved record, keeping the per-row Remove button. The card view model already resolves the scoped fields and each unit's values, so this is a shape change rather than new data. The frontend's populated state is now in the capture and can be worked from directly; DR1's is not, so read app/views/partials/animal-identification-saved-animals.html for the target shape rather than expecting a picture of it.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding DR1's saved animals rendered as a summary list with the identifiers concatenated into one value, rather than as a table with a column per identifier.
finding.correction: The finding stands, with three notes. First, the citation is wrong: app/routes.js:1802-1820 is buildSavedAnimalsTable, which the identification page does not use — the value it produces is read only by the review page (app/routes.js:4342-4348). What the identification page actually renders is app/views/partials/animal-identification-saved-animals.html, included at app/views/animal-identification-details.html:103 and :132, which reads panel.identifierFields and panel.savedAnimals directly. It produces the same thing the finding describes — a header row reading Animal then one cell per identifier label, one row per saved animal keyed by species name and number, and a Remove button in the last cell — so the substance is unaffected, but anyone following the citation lands in the wrong place. Second, the difference slot warns that the frontend's populated state is not in the capture and asks for it to be checked; the same warning is owed to the DR1 side, which is equally unphotographed and equally a reading of a template. Third, understated: DR1's list carries only records whose every identifier is filled (app/routes.js:1622-1624), where the frontend lists every appended unit including ones reading 'No identifier provided'. That difference is a consequence of identification--record-needs-every-identifier rather than separate work. Worth knowing for the build: the frontend already renders this exact shape on the check-answers page, at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/view-model/cards/consignment/species/identifier-table.js:9-24. SECOND PASS, after the state was captured: the frontend's populated state was shot after this finding was written, in two forms — fe-animal-identification-saved with one record and one animal still outstanding, and fe-animal-identification-at-maximum with both records saved. Both show what the frontend slot claimed and the slot now describes the picture. The page model records a `summaryLists` array with one row per animal and an empty `tables` array, so the shape difference is observed rather than inferred, and confidence is raised from medium to high. Two points of accuracy from the capture. The named control resolves: the Remove action is a submit button whose visible text is exactly 'Remove', with ' animal 1' in a visually hidden span after it (``), so a label crop on 'Remove' finds it on both new screens. And the joined value the title quotes was not exercised: the captured records each hold one identifier, so the row reads 'Ear tag: UK123456789012' rather than the two-identifier run-on. The joining is real — summary.js:9-19 maps every filled identifier and joins with ', ' — but the picture shows the shape, not the crowding. DR1's populated panel remains a template read; that is the half of this finding still unphotographed.
